facts.fact: RMS Titanic sank in the early hours of 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg.
Titanic had ten decks for passenger use.
D Deck, the saloon deck, was dominated by the First-Class reception room, the First-Class dining saloon and the Second-Class dining saloon.
An iceberg is a piece of fresh water ice more than 15 meters long that has broken off a glacier or an ice shelf.
About one-tenth of an iceberg’s volume is above water.
Icebergs can capsize as they melt and break apart.
Hypothermia is defined as a body core temperature below 35.0 °C.
Hypothermia can cause confusion and numbness.
A water temperature of 10 °C can kill a human adult in as little as one hour.
There were approximately three million shipwrecks worldwide as of January 1999.
Shipwreck law determines the ownership of a wreck.

sentences.text: Imagine you are aboard the Titanic, unaware of the danger ahead?
Titanic was enormous, measuring 46,329 GRT and 21,831 NRT.
You are on one of its ten decks, enjoying the large dining saloons on D Deck.
Suddenly, the ship strikes an iceberg.
About one-tenth of the iceberg was visible above the water.
The water temperature is near freezing, and it can kill quickly.
Hypothermia sets in when your body temperature drops below 35.0 °C.
You would quickly feel confused and numb as your body fights the cold.
With over three million shipwrecks worldwide, many have faced this same fate.
